runtime: OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM 27.0.1.0.2+1 (Eclipse Adoptium), GC G1, -Xmx2g -XX:+UseG1GC, one JVM per client

results.api: NostrClient.fetch(relay, filter) { event -> } (one REQ, callback per event, returns at EOSE)
results.notes: Quartz's one-relay read on NostrClient, the pool Amethyst runs on, with one relay. fetch hands each event unverified to its callback on the relay's delivery coroutine, nothing collected, deduped or sorted, and returns at EOSE; the callback verifies with Quartz's Event.verify() (id via EventHasher.hashIdCheck, then Schnorr), as Amethyst verifies in LocalCache. Parser: Kite (KiteReader, Quartz's own). The fetch runs in a coroutine on the client's Dispatchers.IO scope. keepConnected() opens the socket in setup, then 1 s to settle: a REQ sent while the new connection replays its filters can go out twice.

results.api: NostrClient.fetch + Quartz's ParallelEventVerifier accessory (batched Event.verify() on Dispatchers.Default)
results.notes: As quartz-fetch, but the callback submits each event to ParallelEventVerifier (default batch 256, parallelism 8), which fans Event.verify() out over Dispatchers.Default and delivers in order. Quartz's documented speed option (an opt-in accessory), so it is a ranked entry of its own, like other libraries' speed options; it verifies on several cores, which the CPU columns show.

All client work runs in Rust: id (verify_id) + signature checked by the relay task before the event is saved to the default in-memory events tracker and announced; a per-client LRU caches verified (id, sig) pairs, so every run builds a new Client. Drops expired (NIP-40) events by design. The notification channel also carries every relay message, so two notifications cross JNA per event, and the EOSE only arrives as a Message notification: the app calls asEnum() on every Message (a clone of the event plus a JNA call, per event) to spot it. ClientBuilder.notificationChannelSize(65536) (default 4096): the broadcast channel drops what a slower reader has not taken yet, and the JNA reader falls behind (with the default, `all` lost 60-65% of its events, a different number every run). alloc_bytes counts only the JVM side (JNA handles, strings); the Rust heap is not counted.

results.api: Client.streamEvents(ReqTarget.single) read with ClientEventStream.next() until it ends at EOSE
results.notes: The short-lived stream API (default exit policy ExitOnEOSE); EOSE = the stream's end. The stream is fed from the relay's own notification broadcast (2048, not settable from the bindings) through a 512-slot channel, so a reader slower than the relay loses events. Otherwise as nostr-sdk-subscribe.

results.api: NostrPool.connectRelay + pool.subscribe(NostrFilter, PassthroughEventTracker::new), setVerifyMatchLocally(false), event/EOSE listeners, sub.open()
results.crypto: Bouncy Castle 1.84 secp256k1 (pure Java, ECAlgorithms.sumOfTwoMultiplies) via nge-platform-jvm's Schnorr; JDK SHA-256
results.notes: NostrRelay verifies every EVENT (id + signature) before listeners see it (verifyEvents, default on), on the common ForkJoinPool (parallelEvents, default on). Subscribes with the library's PassthroughEventTracker (seen() is always false: no per-event dedup set; the pool's default ForwardSlidingWindowEventTracker treats every event older than ~30 min as already seen once 21 events arrived, so a history sync gets ~22 events) and setVerifyMatchLocally(false) (no local re-match of every event against the filter). The pool drops expired (NIP-40) events. Parser: Gson (nge-platform). Needs -Dnge-platforms.allowLoopbackInURIs=true for a loopback relay (set by the harness).

results.websocket: Ktor 3.5.0 WebSockets on the OkHttp engine (OkHttp 5.5.1)
results.notes: The relay client hands over the event's raw JSON; the library's deserializedEvent parses it (kotlinx.serialization) and validates it (Event.isValid: id, then Schnorr), throwing on invalid events (and printing a line for each to stdout). Connects lazily inside request(): the connect is in the timed part. Its filter always carries "kinds":[] (no way to leave it out); the relay ignores filters. Its Tag holds 2-4 strings and deserialization throws on any other length, so valid events with a 1-element or 5+-element tag (imeta, ...) are rejected.
